title: Heat through a conducting partition between a gas at constant volume and a gas at constant pressure: the time for the temperature gap to halve
summary: An insulated container: gas S1 at fixed volume and gas S2 held at atmospheric pressure by a free piston, joined by a conducting partition. The gap decays at rate (16/15) KA/xR, so it halves at t = (15/16) ln 2 xR/KA - n = 0.66 with the given ln 2 = 0.7.
subject: Physics
topic: Heat conduction between a gas at constant volume and a gas at constant pressure - exponential decay of the temperature gap
subtopics: Heat conduction through a slab: H = KA dT/x
Molar heat capacities of a monoatomic gas: C_V = 3R/2 at fixed volume, C_P = 5R/2 at fixed pressure
Two bodies exchanging heat: the gap decays as exp(-(KA/x)(1/C1 + 1/C2) t)
concepts: S1 (rigid) loses heat at constant volume, C_V = 3R/2; S2 (free piston at 1 atm) gains heat at constant pressure, C_P = 5R/2
t_half = (15/16) ln 2 xR/KA: n = 0.656 with ln 2 = 0.7 (0.650 with the exact log), both inside the key
With the piston locked the rate would be 4/3 and n = 0.525: part of S2's heat does work on the piston, so the gap closes more slowly

methods: Solved independently: C_V for S1, C_P for S2; rate (KA/x)(2/3R + 2/5R) = (16/15) KA/xR; t_half = (15/16) ln 2 xR/KA; n = 0.656 with ln 2 = 0.7 (0.650 exact)
sympy: the gap ODE and its solution; t_half = (15/16) ln 2 exactly

First law integrated numerically for each gas with the piston's work from P dV (no C_P assumed): t_half = 0.6498 xR/KA for 100 K and 50 K gaps; heat into S2 splits 3:2 between internal energy and work
Control: locked piston gives 0.525, outside the key - the free piston matters
